NovaBiotech Inc. - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaBiotech Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NovaBiotech's financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Dr. Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Medical Officer; and Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Scientific Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO of NovaBiotech.

Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. NovaBiotech delivered a strong performance in the third quarter, driven by robust revenue growth from our oncology biologics portfolio, including NeoMab-X, our leading PD-1 inhibitor, and accelerating contributions from recent launches like Zephyra and CardioForge. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities, positioning us for sustained leadership in oncology, rare diseases, and beyond.

Today, I will provide an overview of our performance and strategic initiatives, with a focus on our new product launches and the impressive market share gains they're delivering, alongside our strategic priorities and outlook. We are particularly excited about Zephyra, our first-in-class bispecific antibody for relapsed/refractory non-Hodgkin lymphoma, and its potential to redefine treatment paradigms with superior efficacy and safety.

Let me start with updates on our new product launches and market share gains, which have been one of the highlights of the quarter. As you know, we executed two key commercial launches in the past 12 months—Zephyra, which hit the market in the first quarter of this year, and CardioForge, our gene-edited CRISPR-based therapy for familial hypercholesterolemia, which we launched in select EU markets in the second quarter following EMA approval. These launches are already driving outsized revenue growth and positioning us as a leader in next-generation biologics.

In the third quarter alone, Zephyra generated $178 million in net product sales, bringing half-year-to-date sales to $412 million—well ahead of our initial full-year guidance of $350-400 million. This reflects sequential 45% quarter-over-quarter growth, fueled by rapid prescriber adoption. CardioForge, still in its early stages, posted €62 million, approximately $68 million, in EU sales for the quarter, with uptake accelerating after reimbursement wins in Germany and France. Combined, these launches contributed 28% of our total revenue this quarter, up from 12% in the second quarter, and we're on track for peak sales potential exceeding $3.5 billion annually by 2028, according to our updated internal models aligned with IQVIA market at therapy data.

Market share gains have been even more impressive. In the relapsed/refractory non-Hodgkin lymphoma segment—a market dominated by Roche's Gazyva and Bristol Myers Squibb's Yescarta—Zephyra has captured 22% U.S. market share by new-to-brand prescriptions within nine months of launch, per Symphony Health data through week 39. That's triple the typical launch velocity for bispecifics, outpacing even Regeneron's Libtayo in comparable oncology introductions. Total prescription share now stands at 14%, with an eight-point sequential gain. We're seeing strong traction in community oncology settings, where Zephyra's once-monthly subcutaneous dosing and cleaner safety profile—65% lower rates of cytokine release syndrome compared to competitor CAR-T therapies—are resonating strongly. Payer mix is favorable as well: 78% commercial coverage, including step-edit wins at CVS Caremark and Express Scripts, with 62% Medicare Part D penetration.

The U.S. accounts for 85% of Zephyra sales, but we're advancing internationally. In Europe, Zephyra launched via our AstraZeneca partnership in the third quarter, generating €45 million in initial uptake across five key markets and grabbing 11% share in the aggressive NHL subcategory per IQVIA MIDAS. Asia-Pacific follows next, with a Japan PMDA filing on track for first-half 2025 approval and a co-promotion deal with Takeda targeting 15-20% share in their home market within two years. For CardioForge, EU performance is outstanding—19% share in heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia versus Regeneron's Evkeeza—driven by our proprietary lipid nanoparticle delivery technology, which enables durable LDL-C reductions of 72% at 12 months from the pivotal Phase 3 AETHER trial. China NMPA approval is expected in the fourth quarter of 2024, backed by a $500 million upfront from our WuXi Biologics joint venture to support regional manufacturing.

On the supply side, we've derisked aggressively. Our Singapore biologics facility, now at 120,000 liters capacity after Phase 3 expansion, achieved 99.5% yield on Zephyra lots this quarter, avoiding the raw material shortages that impacted peers like Seagen's ADC launches. We've also filed for a supplemental NDA in the U.S. for Zephyra's frontline NHL label expansion, with ATLAS-2 study data showing a 48% objective response rate versus 32% for standard rituximab combinations—potentially adding another $1 billion in peak sales. For CardioForge, our CRISPR-Cas13 platform is progressing into combinations with PCSK9 inhibitors, with preclinical data at ESC 2024 demonstrating synergistic 85% LDL reductions.

These gains highlight our shift to precision oncology and rare cardio-metabolics, where biosimilar risks are low—unlike the GLP-1 arena facing 20-30% pricing pressure from copycats. We're using real-world evidence from our Zephyra patient registry, now with 4,200 enrollees, to secure NCCN guideline inclusion, which could push share to 30% by year-end. Competitively, we're eroding the Keytruda/Opdivo dominance in lymphoma adjuvants through dual CD20/CD3 engagement for better B-cell depletion.

Turning to our strategic priorities and outlook, which anchor our disciplined execution in a biotech landscape with accelerating cell and gene therapy innovation, U.S. pricing pressures, and strong demand for advanced oncology assets. In the third quarter, we achieved 28% year-over-year revenue growth to $2.22 billion, powered by 25% volume growth in NovaLumab—our PD-1 blockbuster mirroring Merck's Keytruda trajectory but with a superior safety profile in MSI-high tumors, now at $4.2 billion in trailing 12-month sales. Our biosimilars, led by NovaFilgrastim, added $280 million, securing 22% U.S. share amid Neulasta patent expirations. Non-GAAP EPS hit $2.50, beating consensus by 8%, with adjusted operating margins up 320 basis points to 38% on Singapore manufacturing efficiencies.

For fiscal 2024 and beyond, our priorities rest on four pillars: pipeline acceleration, portfolio diversification, global scale, and capital discipline.

Pipeline acceleration targets high-unmet-need areas. NovaLumab's frontline NSCLC combo with bispecific NovaBispec-101 heads to Phase 3 topline in the second quarter of 2025—interim data showed 42% overall response rate and 14-month progression-free survival, eyeing $2.5 billion peak sales against Roche's Tecentriq. NovaCAR-BCMA advances in pivotal trials for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma, with 85% enrollment of 320 patients and BLA submission in the second half of 2025. Three gene-edited assets via our Editas Medicine CRISPR collaboration include NovaEdit-HBB for beta-thalassemia, IND cleared in the fourth quarter of 2023, plus two oncology knockouts. R&D rises modestly to 22% of revenue, or $2.8 billion for fiscal 2024, focusing on programs with over 60% success probability—we project four new molecular entities by 2027.

Portfolio diversification extends beyond oncology, 72% of revenue, into rare diseases and immunology. IL-23 inhibitor NovaRheum-456 offers better psoriasis skin clearance than Janssen's Tremfya, with PASI-90 at 78% versus 65%; EU approval in first-quarter 2025, U.S. PDUFA mid-year, $1.2 billion peak potential. NovaGene-AAV for spinal muscular atrophy hits Phase 2b, priced like Zolgensma at $2.8 million per dose with enhanced CNS penetration. Biosimilars drive $1.5 billion in fiscal 2024 growth, launching five more by 2026—including adalimumab and ustekinumab analogs—at 30% EBITDA margins.

Global scale sees U.S. revenue at 65%, up 22% projected for fiscal 2024 on stable IRA pricing for NovaLumab at $145,000 net ASP per course despite 12% list discounts. Europe at 22% benefits from two EMA biosimilar nods amid HTA challenges; we're piloting value-based pricing in Germany's AMNOG. Asia-Pacific jumps 35% year-over-year to $180 million on China NMPA for NovaLumab generics and a $500 million Innovent partnership for ADCs, like AstraZeneca's Enhertu. A $400 million Suzhou fill-finish plant cuts COGS 15%, aiming for 50% APAC mix by 2027. LATAM grows 40% via access programs.

Capital discipline guides free cash flow at $3.2-3.5 billion for fiscal 2024, 45% margin, funding $2.0 billion buybacks and 20% dividend increase to $1.20 per share. Net debt/EBITDA at 1.8x enables $1-3 billion M&A, like our $850 million Point Biopharma radiopharma deal. No major dilution; 4% shares repurchased year-to-date.

For fiscal 2024, revenue guides $5.1-5.3 billion, 17-20% growth; core EPS $7.40-7.70, up 15%; Q4 revenue $1.35-1.45 billion. Risks like PBM rebates are buffered 90% gross-to-net. Long-term, 12-15% CAGR to 2028, oncology and rare diseases to $12 billion peak, ahead of Regeneron.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Chen, our CFO, for a detailed financial review.

Mike Chen, CFO:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex highlighted, we had a solid third quarter. Revenue reached $2.22 billion, up 28% compared to the same period last year, primarily driven by volume growth in NeoMab-X, contributions from new launches like Zephyra, and biosimilar uptake.

Our GAAP net income was $500 million, or $2.10 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $600 million, or $2.50 per share.

Operating expenses totaled $1.5 billion, reflecting continued investments in R&D to advance our pipeline while benefiting from manufacturing scale. We remain committed to these investments. Our cash position is strong at $1.8 billion.

As we look at the full year, we're updating guidance to revenue of $5.1-5.3 billion, core EPS $7.40-7.70, and free cash flow $3.2-3.5 billion.

Let me dive deeper into some key financial aspects, starting with gross margin trends and manufacturing efficiency—one of our core strengths. Gross margins for the quarter came in at 87.2%, up 420 basis points sequentially from 83.0% in Q2 and 510 basis points year-over-year from 82.1% in Q3 2023. This is our 10th straight quarter of expansion, with trailing 12-month average at 86.1%—surpassing the large-cap biotech peer average of 78% per Evaluate Pharma.

Cost of goods sold as a percentage of net product sales fell to 12.8% from 17.0% in Q2 and 17.9% year-over-year. Absolute COGS grew just 2% to $285 million despite 28% topline growth, thanks to multi-year manufacturing investments.

Key drivers include yield improvements and process optimization, contributing about 300 basis points. Our 200,000-liter facilities in Devens, Massachusetts, and Singapore boosted average bioreactor titers 22% year-over-year to 8.2 grams per liter for antibodies like NeoMab-X, via CRISPR-Cas9 cell line engineering—well above BioPlan Associates' 4-6 g/L CHO benchmarks. Downstream purification efficiency rose with 15% better Protein A resin productivity, cycle times down from 48 to 41 hours using Cytiva's multimodal resins, saving $45 million annually on NeoMab-X.

We've also shifted to continuous manufacturing, adding 150 basis points. Our first integrated continuous line at Devens for EvoCell-7 CAR-T, using GE Healthcare ÄKTA flow and Sartorius single-use, cut cost per dose 31% to $28,000 from $41,000, hitting 95% utilization versus peers' 70%. We aim for 40% of biologics volume on continuous by end-2025, ahead of Roche.

Raw material and supply chain efficiencies added 100 basis points: API costs down 8% via offtake deals with AGC and WuXi, single-use at 85% upstream cutting cleaning OPEX 12% and water 40%. Fill-finish COGS dropped 18% at Athlone, Ireland, with Bosch FLC 3000 isolators at 120,000 vials per shift.

Regionally: U.S. at 91.5%, up 600 basis points on payer mix and stable pricing; Europe at 82.3% despite biosimilar pressures in Germany/France; ex-U.S./Asia at 84.7%, Singapore offsetting China discounts via Samsung partnership.

These build on our Manufacturing 2027 roadmap, $450 million over three years for 3x ROI. Initiatives include AI-driven PAT with Thermo Fisher Raman for 10-15% yield gains, biosimilar defense for NeoMab-X post-2028 at sub-$5,000 per gram COGS, and 100,000-liter Jurong expansion by Q4 2025. Q4 margins guide 88-89%, fiscal 2024 86.5-87%, 550 basis points expansion. Risks like Red Sea inflation are buffered; long-term, 90%+ margins protect 50% EBITDA.

Next, the pricing and reimbursement landscape, critical for sustainability amid payer scrutiny and biosimilars. U.S., 62% of Q3 sales up 4% year-over-year, saw 5.2% WAC growth per SSR Health, ASP at 92% of WAC. For NovaKine, our GLP-1/GIP agonist, 6.8% January WAC hike positioned it versus Mounjaro/Ozempic; rebates at 48%, but outcomes-based on 25% lives limit erosion to 1.2%. Oncura ADC faced 2.1% ASP dip from Enhertu competition, stabilized by Medicare Advantage and assistance programs.

IRA caps loom for 2026 small molecules, but $250 million RWE investment preps ICER wins. Europe, 22% sales, ASP up 3.7%: NovaKine on 14/17 formularies, NICE at £145,000/QALY; Germany IQWiG "considerable benefit" for Oncura at €78,000 via MEA. France HAS 65%, Italy AIFA conversions. Biosimilars erode anti-TNFs 35%, but data exclusivity shields us; new MEAs like pay-over-time for GeneFix.

Ex-U.S. emerging: Japan 11% ASP growth, Australia PBS at A$950/week. China NRDL 72% cut for NovaKine exploded volumes 150% to $120 million run-rate; Oncura CDE targets 2025.

Our value-over-volume strategy: 70% contracts performance-based, 340B at 95%, $50 million copay fund. FY24 net price 4-6%, gross-to-net 39-41%. Biosimilars erode $20 billion originators by 2025, but next-gen like NovaBis sustains premiums.

Finally, cash flow and balance sheet highlights. Cash, equivalents, and short-term investments ended at $1.8 billion, up 25% sequentially to over 3.5-year runway. Unrestricted $1.65 billion. Debt $750 million, net $420 million or 0.15x TTM EBITDA. Inventory 8 months, DSO 52 days; intangibles $4.2 billion including $800 million Helix IPR&D.

Q3 OCF $620 million, up 40%; TTM $1.1 billion at 38% margins from AETH-301 NSCLC share and Roche upfronts. FCF $480 million post-$140 million capex (Singapore expansion). Investing $320 million, R&D capex $220 million year-to-date on AI discovery. Financing $50 million inflow.

FY24 OCF $2.0-2.3 billion, FCF $1.4-1.7 billion funds R&D, $400 million buybacks, tuck-in M&A. Risks like biosimilars offset by milestones.

For the full year, guidance as noted. Now, I'll turn to Dr. Elena Vasquez, our Chief Medical Officer, for clinical updates.

Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Medical Officer:
Thank you, Mike. We're thrilled with clinical progress. NovaLumab's NSCLC combo with NovaBispec-101 shows 42% ORR interim; topline Q2 2025. NovaCAR-BCMA 85% enrolled, BLA H2 2025. NovaEdit-HBB IND cleared; NovaRheum-456 Phase 3 PASI-90 78%; NovaGene-AAV Phase 2b. Zephyra sNDA frontline NHL ORR 48%; CardioForge combos preclinical 85% LDL drop. We expect multiple milestones: two Phase 3 starts, one approval Q4.

Now, back to Alex.

Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you, Elena. We will now open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from David Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Lee, Goldman Sachs:
Thanks. Mike, on gross margins, can you expand on continuous manufacturing scalability and potential risks from FDA validation?

Mike Chen, CFO:
Great question, David. Our Devens continuous line for EvoCell-7 is at 95% utilization, cost per dose $28,000. Scaling to 40% volume by 2025 leverages Sartorius and GE tech, ahead of peers. FDA validation on track Q1 2025; we've got six-month inventory buffers for disruptions. This supports 88-89% Q4 margins.

Operator:
Our next question from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen, JPMorgan:
Alex, on new launches, how sustainable are Zephyra's share gains versus CAR-T competition?

Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO:
Lisa, Zephyra's 22% NBRx share reflects 65% lower CRS and subQ dosing. ATLAS-2 frontline data 48% ORR positions $1 billion uplift. RWE registry drives NCCN inclusion to 30% year-end. Unlike CAR-T CAPEX, our model scales profitably.

Operator:
Our next question from Mark Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mark Patel, Morgan Stanley:
Mike, pricing outlook with IRA and China NRDL—any updates?

Mike Chen, CFO:
Mark, U.S. net ASP stable via outcomes rebates; IRA buffered by RWE for 2026. China NRDL volumes up 150% post-72% cut, $120 million run-rate. FY24 4-6% net growth affirmed.

Operator:
Our next question from Sarah Kim with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Sarah Kim, Bank of America:
On strategic outlook, pipeline prioritization details?

Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Medical Officer:
Sarah, 60%+ PoS focus: NovaCAR-BCMA pivotal complete soon, BLA H2 2025; NovaBispec NSCLC topline Q2 2025. Diversification via NovaRheum EU Q1 2025, biosimilars five launches.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes questions at this time.

Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue executing on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NovaBiotech Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
